title: Financial Systems: The Finance Stack and Who Owns It
summary: What financial systems are, the layers of the modern finance stack (ERP, data, close, planning, agents), who owns them, and how that role is becoming the finance engineer.
body_markdown:
Behind every finance team is a stack of software, the **financial systems** that record transactions, close the books, plan the budget, manage cash, and produce reporting. How well that stack is chosen, connected, and run increasingly determines how well the finance function performs. And the job of owning it, once a quiet back-office responsibility, is turning into one of the most important roles in finance.


This guide explains what financial systems are, the layers of the modern finance stack, who owns them, and how that role is changing.


## **What are financial systems?**


Financial systems are the software tools and platforms a company uses to run its finance and accounting operations, recording transactions, closing the books, planning, managing cash, ensuring controls, and reporting. Together they form the "finance stack." The term spans the system of record (the ERP) and all the specialized tools around it, plus the integrations that connect them so data flows instead of being re-keyed.


> A company's financial systems are the plumbing of the finance function. When the stack is well-chosen and well-connected, data flows and the team does real work. When it is not, the team spends its days moving numbers between tools by hand.


## **The layers of the modern finance stack**


- **System of record (ERP).** The general ledger and core accounting, NetSuite, QuickBooks, SAP, Sage Intacct, where the numbers officially live.
- **The data layer.** The data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) plus the banking, billing, and CRM systems that feed finance.
- **Close and controls.** Reconciliation, close management, and controls tools that turn the ledger into trustworthy statements.
- **Planning and analysis.** FP&A and planning tools for budgeting, forecasting, and variance.
- **Treasury and payments.** Cash management, treasury, and AP/AR tools that move and track money.
- **The agent layer.** The newest layer: AI agents that run work across all of the above. See[agentic ERP](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/agentic-erp) .


The hard part is rarely any single system, it is the connections between them. Real finance work spans layers (a reconciliation touches the ERP, the bank, and a subledger), so a stack is only as good as how well its systems talk to each other.


## **Who owns financial systems?**


Ownership of the finance stack has traditionally been fragmented or treated as an afterthought:


- **A finance systems or FinOps analyst.** In larger companies, a dedicated role administers the ERP and finance tools, manages integrations, and supports the team.
- **The controller or a finance lead.** In many companies, the controller or a finance manager owns the systems alongside their other work.
- **IT, partially.** IT often owns procurement and security, while finance owns day-to-day use, a split that can leave gaps.


However it is divided, the role has historically been about keeping the systems running and the data flowing, more administration than strategy.


## **How the role is changing: from systems owner to finance engineer**


That is shifting. As AI agents become a layer of the finance stack, the person who owns financial systems is no longer just administering tools, they are building and operating the systems that do the work. The job moves from "keep the ERP running and the integrations alive" to "design and supervise the agents and workflows that run the close, forecasting, and reporting across the stack."


That is the emergence of the[finance engineer](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/finance-engineer) : the finance professional who treats the finance stack as something to build on, not just maintain. The finance systems role is becoming a builder role, and it is one of the highest-leverage seats in the modern[office of the CFO](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/office-of-the-cfo) .


This is also why the agent layer matters so much to the stack. A platform like[Concourse](https://www.concourse.ai/) connects across the ERP, data warehouse, and banking systems and runs the work on top, so the person who owns financial systems can operate the whole function through one layer rather than stitching tools together by hand, with every number traceable to source.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What are financial systems?**


Financial systems are the software tools a company uses to run finance and accounting, recording transactions, closing the books, planning, managing cash, and reporting, plus the integrations that connect them. Together they form the finance stack, spanning the ERP and the specialized tools around it.


### **What is in a modern finance stack?**


The system of record (ERP), the data layer (warehouse plus banking, billing, and CRM), close and controls tools, planning and analysis (FP&A) tools, treasury and payments tools, and increasingly an AI agent layer that runs work across all of them. The connections between systems matter as much as the systems themselves.


### **Who owns financial systems?**


Traditionally a finance systems or FinOps analyst, the controller, or a finance lead, often with IT owning procurement and security. The role has historically been about keeping systems running and data flowing, though it is now evolving toward a builder role.


### **How is the finance systems role changing?**


As AI agents become part of the finance stack, the systems owner is shifting from administering tools to building and operating the agents and workflows that run the work. This is the emergence of the finance engineer, a builder role rather than a maintenance one.


## **The bottom line**


Financial systems are the stack that runs the finance function, ERP, data, close, planning, treasury, and now an agent layer, and the connections between them matter as much as the tools. Owning that stack used to mean keeping it running. It is becoming a builder role, the finance engineer, as AI agents turn the stack from something you maintain into something you build on.
